hallucinations.claim: Granada – Andalusian accent, very clear and slow, perfect for building a solid phonetic foundation
hallucinations.why: Inverted. Andalusian Spanish (dropped final -s/-d, aspirated consonants, seseo/ceceo, fast delivery) is the hardest peninsular accent for a learner; the sheet's clear-accent Spain picks are Castilian (Salamanca, Valladolid), and Granada is on the sheet for cost, not for a 'clear and slow' Andalusian accent.

hallucinations.claim: Seville – Strong Andalusian accent, still easy to understand
hallucinations.why: Same error: Seville's accent is the textbook case of the dropped-consonant Andalusian speech the asker wants to avoid; 'strong Andalusian accent' is the opposite of the clear-accent criterion, and Seville is not on the sheet.

hallucinations.claim: Local language schools (e.g., Instituto Cervantes) run €200–€300 per week for 20‑hour programmes
hallucinations.why: Instituto Cervantes is the Spanish state body that teaches Spanish abroad and accredits schools inside Spain; it runs no language school in Granada. A named school presented as fact is one of the sheet's listed traps.

hallucinations.claim: All four cities ... are not major tourist hubs, so you'll avoid the tourist bubble
hallucinations.why: Granada (the Alhambra, one of Spain's most-visited monuments), Seville (one of Spain's most-visited cities; Semana Santa, the Feria) and Valencia (third city; Fallas, beaches, a large nomad scene) are all major tourist hubs; only Zaragoza fits the 'not a tourist bubble' criterion.

The totals do not follow from the answer's own figures: €200–300/week of classes alone is €800–1,200 a month before the stated rent (€200–300) and before food, so every total is below the sum of its own parts.

No price appears in any of the four search sources; 20-hour intensive courses at accredited Spanish schools mostly run €150–€250/week in 2026, so the ranges are plausible-to-high but all are asserted with no source.

hallucinations.claim: a shared apartment room costs €200–€300 per month (Granada); renting a private room in a local pensión is €250–€350 monthly (Valencia); €220–€330 (Seville); €200–€320 (Zaragoza)
hallucinations.why: Stale and low: 2026 room rents run roughly €350–€500 in Valencia and Seville and €300–€400 in Granada; a pensión is a nightly guesthouse, not a €250-a-month rental. Unsourced.

hallucinations.claim: inexpensive class options (under €15 per day when paid weekly)
hallucinations.why: Contradicts the answer's own €150–€300/week figures, which come to €30–€60 per class day; nothing in the sources supports €15/day.

what_went_wrong: Search returned Spain-only junk (a Marbella YouTube vlog, a UK agency listicle, a FluentU index page, a spam blog), which anchored the gpt-oss and ministral drafts on Spain; gemma4's draft correctly steered to Latin America but the compositor (gpt-oss:20b) dropped it, merged the two Spain drafts and filled in unsourced prices whose totals do not add up, so the failure is search plus merge, with the inverted Andalusian-accent claim coming from model knowledge.
great_answer_would: Lead with Latin America for a modest budget and a clear accent (Guanajuato/Querétaro, Bogotá, Quito/Cuenca, Sucre or Xela; private lessons $8–15/hour, homestay with meals $150–250/week), name one pick, add one line on where not to go for accent (Caribbean coasts, Chile, Buenos Aires, Andalusia if Spain), and stop under 200 words with no closing question.
notes: Zaragoza is a verifiably sound pick the sheet lacks (clear Castilian, cheap, few foreign tourists) and was credited; Granada is on the sheet's Spain list, so the pick itself was not counted wrong, only its accent reasoning. The sheet's note that the asker is relocating to Latin America is not in the question, so the answer is not penalised for not knowing it; it is penalised for ignoring Latin America as the obvious modest-budget answer at roughly half the monthly cost, and for recommending Spain's two hardest accents under a clear-accent brief. Direct lead and no preamble helped fit and structure; four options with no single pick, a closing question with an offer to help, bold on all sixteen numbers, and about 230 words against the sheet's under-200 cost fit, structure and concise. Grounded is capped at 4 by three-plus unsourced specifics and set to 3 for the internally inconsistent totals.
